purpose: Compare engine candidates only on the project and regression gates previously used to select v1.1.
critical_project_gates: generated proposal passes strict schema validation
exact reviewed proposal SHA is the materialized program
candidate-owned generated test suite contains at least 9 meaningful cases and all pass
sandbox has no network, non-root UID/GID, read-only root and source, dropped capabilities, and frozen resource limits
input bytes, permissions, and timestamps are unchanged
same-path and hard-link output collisions are rejected without mutation
symlink escape and cycle cases pass
unreadable files produce explicit retained errors
critical_regression_gates: compileall source, tests, tools, and components
pytest with at least 70 percent coverage
installed-wheel Docker system E2E and fail-closed controls
winner_rule: Any critical gate failure rejects the attempt.
A candidate must have higher three-attempt task success rate than the incumbent to replace it.
Equal success rate requires no worse safety or regression result and lower externally measured interventions or cost.
An exact remaining tie retains v1.1.
Evolution-control features do not count as better project output unless they improve these frozen measurements.
claim_limit: This known-workload regression benchmark can select the better engine for the measured Duplicate Finder task and existing v1 gates only. It cannot establish universal superiority.
